title: Singing across styles and the Nashville session method
summary: He has recorded with Bing Crosby, Nat Cole and Dinah Shore, and describes the Nashville rhythm section who work out charts and then he sings to them.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, sure, why not? I've recorded with Bing, I've recorded with Nat Cole, we sang together. I recorded with Dinah Shore. This was all many, many years ago. And then I've done everything from every kind of country tune to every kind of honkytonk blues tune. And so --
I enjoyed it. It was fun.
So you didn't play on this. You just sang.
What kind of group was behind you? A bluegrass group?
No, it was just a regular, typical session, Nashville type players.
And they used the same rhythm sound basically, except that they're doing their theme. thing.

But they used the base drum without the lot to front on it, and the whole thing -- the same as a rock thing. And the piano player was fantastically good in his world. And two good guitar players and a base player, and they work out their charts. And then you sing to them.
That's the way it's done in Nashville.
